messages:
anya: quick sanity-check — after the RFC, i'm trying to land a concrete contract for the runtime's fused-attention variant selection. main questions: deterministic outputs across fused vs non-fused, where to draw the compat boundary, and how much the runtime should enforce dropout-free inference paths.

sahil: +1. can we start by enumerating guarantees we need? eg: shape/strides, kv-cache layout, numeric equivalence (within eps), and fallback semantics.

kevin: i think we should guarantee: 1) identical return shapes and dtypes 2) kv cache binary layout compatibility when using dedicated kv-transfer ops 3) documented max-sequence behavior. we can't promise bitwise identical floats because of fused kernel reorderings.

maria: agree with kevin. also add: deterministic RNG for dropoutless path must be opt-in. we should have a strict 'inference' flag that disables all dropout at graph / kernel-level so results are stable across kernel variants.

anya: proposal: runtime exposes selection policy with 3 modes: "strict-compat" (software fallback if kernel deviates), "best-effort" (prefer fused kernels, emit warn metric if mismatch), "perf-first" (always pick fastest compatible kernel ignoring small numeric deltas). thoughts?

jamie: maybe rename "strict-compat" -> "bitwise-compat"? but kevin said bitwise identical isn't possible. so "semantically-compatible"? i prefer short names: compat, best_effort, perf.

kevin: semantics: compat = same numerical tolerances & same cache layout; we should get an eval harness that compares outputs across a corpus of prompts and reports regression rates. if >X% diffs then kernel gets flagged.

infra-bot: perf-test/ci: fused-qkv-ci triggered for branch:feat/attn-contracts — run started (build 47). ETA ~12m. :gear:

maria: runtime API question: where lives the contract check? at kernel registration time (so we reject registering a kernel that doesn't declare compat capabilities) OR at instantiation time (so we can pick per-model/per-config). prefer instantiation-time checks so we can have model-specific tolerances.

sahil: instantiation-time + a per-model policy sounds best. model metadata can include "tolerance_profile": low/medium/high. low = strict numerics, high = allow more numeric drift.

anya: what about bias+rope fusion? i've seen variance in rope implementation ordering affecting outputs slightly. do we require a canonical rope op in the runtime to normalize?

kevin: yes — define a canonical rope transform API in the kernel interface and require kernels to either implement it or call our canonical routine. that avoids duplication. small note: this needs to be fast; calling out-of-line code may cost perf.

jamie: maybe a hybrid: canonical math but allow in-kernel optimized path if you pass a tiny conformance test. runtime can run a short microtest at kernel load to assert equivalence within tolerance.

maria: dropout-free: we should expose `inference_mode=true` on session and allow kernels to skip masked-dropout computations entirely. critical for tiny-latency SLOs. also need to make sure quantized kernels get same math ordering.

anya: fallback semantics: if compat-mode and kernel fails conformance, do we fallback to reference (slower) kernel, or fatal? i vote fallback + alert + canary quota shrink for that kernel.

sahil: fallback + metric + auto-blacklist after N failures. also add a hook for devs to opt their kernel back in once they push a fix.

kevin: operation edge cases: model pinned to a specific kernel version should ignore auto-blacklist (enterprise behaviour). add an override flag on route config.

infra-bot: perf-test/ci: fused-qkv-ci build 47 finished. summary: 2 regressions, 120ms tail latency improvement on a 2048 seq. artifacts: https://ci.redwood.dev/build/47 :white_check_mark:

maria: nice. can we add a small binary-diff tool that hashes concatenated float outputs with tolerance bucketing so we can triage quickly?

jamie: I'll sketch `tolerant-digest` CLI: accepts baseline and candidate outputs, tolerance profile, returns pass/fail + top-k diffs. can also produce a minimal repro prompt.

anya: action items: 1) jamie to prototype tolerant-digest + microtest harness (ETA 1w) 2) kevin to draft kernel interface change for canonical rope op + conformance API (ETA 2w) 3) sahil/maria to outline runtime policy enums and blacklist workflow (ETA 1w) 4) infra to wire ci to emit conformance report (infra acknowledged).

kevin: also: document expected numeric eps by dtype (fp16/fp32/int8) in the model catalog so product teams can pick tolerance profiles proactively.

anya: sounds good. one last ask — let's log an example config snippet for the route API in this thread so integrations have something to copy.

jamie: paste:```json
{"route": "/chat", "model": "ggml-redwood-v1", "kernel_policy": "compat", "inference_mode": true, "tolerance_profile": "low"}
```

maria: perfect. thanks all. i'll follow up with a short RFC addendum summarizing the decisions. :sparkles:
